topic: What if Mihawk had killed Zoro at the Baratie, and how that erases the lesson Zoro uses on Sommers
title: What If Zoro Died Against Mihawk?
description:
What if Zoro never survived his duel with Dracule Mihawk at the Baratie? No Kuraigana training, no Mihawk lesson, no clean Supreme King Haki cut on Shepherd Sommers in chapter 1194. Follow the chain from Arlong Park to Thriller Bark to Elbaph and see who pays.

Who do you think pays the most: Luffy, Mihawk or Elbaph? And if you liked the Gum-Gum Fruit story, this is the same kind of strict cause and effect, one change and everything that follows.
comment: Is Zoro's loss to Mihawk the most important fight in the whole story, or is Luffy the only fixed point that matters? Pick one.

lines.text: Mihawk's black blade cuts across Zoro's chest, and this time, nobody pulls him out of the sea.

shot.fallback: green haired swordsman collapsing into dark sea water, black blade overhead

lines.text: No second chance, no Johnny and Yosaku dragging him up, no wounded swordsman grinning through the blood.

shot.search: Zoro Mihawk Baratie falls into sea
shot.fallback: green haired swordsman collapsing into dark sea water, black blade overhead

lines.text: So what happens to the Straw Hats, and to Elbaph, when the swordsman is gone before the story even starts?

shot.fallback: green haired swordsman collapsing into dark sea water, black blade overhead

lines.text: But in this version, Zoro dies at the Baratie before he lands one real cut on the title he promised to take.

shot.fallback: green haired swordsman collapsing into dark sea water, black blade overhead

lines.text: I don't think this is about one missing fighter. I think the whole crew bends around the hole...

shot.fallback: green haired swordsman collapsing into dark sea water, black blade overhead

lines.text: And the man holding that black blade is the same man whose lesson Zoro just used in chapter 1194.

shot.fallback: green haired swordsman collapsing into dark sea water, black blade overhead

lines.text: Which means this fight at the Baratie is where Elbaph's biggest problem either gets solved, or never gets solved at all.

shot.fallback: green haired swordsman collapsing into dark sea water, black blade overhead

lines.text: Pull that one thread, and the Straw Hats come apart one island at a time...

shot.fallback: green haired swordsman collapsing into dark sea water, black blade overhead

lines.text: Start at the Baratie, because it's the first thing that changes. Luffy is there to recruit a cook, and he leaves with grief.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: In the story we know, Luffy throws an arm at Mihawk the second Zoro falls, and Mihawk tells him Zoro hasn't died.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: Here, Mihawk says nothing like that. Luffy stands on a broken deck, holding a hat, with one crewmate already gone.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: I think this is the moment Luffy learns what the sea actually costs, and he learns it in the Baratie arc, long before Marineford.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: Sanji watches all of it from the kitchen. He still has a restaurant, a debt to Zeff, and a bad reason to stay.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: Don Krieg is still on the ship, and Luffy beats him anyway, because Krieg never needed Zoro to lose.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: That part of canon doesn't care. Luffy's rubber body and his rage are enough for a pirate fleet.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: And Sanji still leaves with Luffy, since Zeff's push toward the sea doesn't depend on Zoro either.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: Zeff watches Sanji pack, and he never mentions the dead swordsman. He just tells him to go and see the sea.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: Johnny and Yosaku, the two bounty hunters who worshipped Zoro, hear the news, and I think they quit the whole business.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: Luffy doesn't cry on screen. Luffy never does. He just pulls his hat low and keeps walking.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: But the crew that sails out of the Baratie is quieter, and nobody on that ship is chasing the same dream anymore.

shot.search: Straw Hats Going Merry Nami Usopp
shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: Because Zoro wasn't just the muscle. He was the one person who said out loud what Luffy was too proud to.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: After losing, Zoro told his captain he would never lose again until he beat the world's best swordsman.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: That promise started years earlier with a girl named Kuina and a vow that one of them would be number one.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: Now Kuina's sword, Wado Ichimonji, never gets the chance to cut anything but a sea-soaked deck.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: I want you to hold onto that sword, because it comes back in a very uncomfortable way near the end.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: For now, the Going Merry sails on with one crewmate fewer, and Arlong Park is the next thing in the road.

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: But Arlong Park was never a fight a rubber arm could win alone. So who is left to stand in the way?

shot.fallback: Luffy in a straw hat shouting in rage on a restaurant ship deck

lines.text: Arlong Park matters because it's personal. It's Nami's village, Nami's debt, and Nami's lie that Luffy finally breaks.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: In the story we know, Zoro fights Hatchan there with the Mihawk wound barely closed, and he still wins.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: Six swords on Hatchan's side, one bleeding swordsman on Zoro's, and Zoro wins it anyway.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: Take Zoro out, and Hatchan is still standing, while Sanji and Usopp have to carry fights they were never meant to carry.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: Sanji beats Kuroobi in canon, so that fight holds. The cracks only show where Zoro was the only answer.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: Usopp is the proof of how that goes. He fights Chew, and he wins by being clever, not by being strong.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: Luffy still takes Arlong down, because that fight was never about a swordsman. It's about Nami's hat and Luffy's promise.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: He puts the straw hat on her head, and Nami joins. That beat survives, and I'll give canon credit for that.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: So the early voyage mostly holds together. Luffy still reaches Loguetown, Smoker still chases, and Dragon's storm still saves him.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: The first real gap shows up in Alabasta, a desert war that needs a crew with every single piece in place.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: Zoro's job there was Mr. 1, a swordsman whose body turns to steel.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: Zoro's answer was to cut steel itself, listening for the breath of the metal, and he did it in one stroke.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: Without Zoro in that desert, Baroque Works keeps a steel blade nobody has found a way to answer.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: My read is that Vivi's rebels pay for it. Not the main plot, just the fights nobody was supposed to lose.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: Luffy still beats Crocodile in the end, but he does it carrying the weight of everyone who went down on the way.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: And the crew keeps climbing, from Skypiea to Water 7 to Enies Lobby, looking a little more like a team of survivors.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: People will say that's exaggerating, because Luffy's crew always finds a way. Fair, and canon supports them.

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: But the crew in canon finds its way because its swordsman is always the one standing at the door. Who stands there now?

shot.fallback: dark island with fishman pirates and a roaring crowd

lines.text: Skip ahead to Thriller Bark, where the crew gets smashed down and a Warlord named Kuma shows up out of the fog.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: Kuma goes for Luffy's life, and the crew has nothing left to stop him.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: In canon, Zoro offers his own life, and Kuma pulls the pain out of Luffy and pushes it into Zoro instead.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: Then Sanji asks what happened, and Zoro answers with the two most famous words in the whole crew's history.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: Nothing happened. Nothing at all.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: Even Oda went back to that scene later, because chapter 1097 shows Kuma taking other people's pain in a flashback.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: Now take Zoro out of the picture, and the question gets ugly. Who stands in front of Kuma and takes it?

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: Luffy has just taken a brutal beating fighting the zombie giant Oars, so the pain stacked on him is the whole problem.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: Zoro even swung at Kuma before that, which tells you he was always ready to stand in front of Luffy.

shot.search: Zoro Kuma Thriller Bark Lion Song
shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: That scene exists to show the crew's loyalty runs through a person, not a rule.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: I think Sanji tries, because that's who Sanji is. But Kuma's test was about loyalty, and loyalty has a face.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: And if nobody takes that pain, Luffy takes it himself, which means the captain is out of the story right there.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: That sets up Sabaody, where Kuma scatters them anyway, except this time he scatters a crew that already knows it has a hole.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: Two years later, each crewmate comes back with a new level of strength, and the time skip becomes a big deal.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: Luffy trains with Rayleigh. Sanji goes to the Kamabakka Queendom, and everybody becomes something they weren't.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: Zoro, in canon, gets sent to an island of ghosts and goes to the one man he lost to, asking him for a lesson.

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: And now, in this story, nobody walks into Kuraigana asking for anything. So what does the world's greatest swordsman do?

shot.fallback: Thriller Bark gothic ship with a giant bear shape in the fog

lines.text: Think about what Kuraigana looks like. Mihawk, a castle of ghosts, and Perona, who lives there because Kuma sent her.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: It's quiet. Mihawk is the best swordsman on earth, and no one has ever asked him for anything.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: In canon, Zoro asks for a lesson. The proudest swordsman on earth asks for help, and he asks anyway.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: Mihawk even asks his name at the Baratie, so he keeps the name of the kid who refused to run.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: In canon, someone finally does, and Mihawk agrees. That's the part I keep thinking about.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: Mihawk spent two years teaching the swordsman who swore to take his title. That makes no sense for a man who hates weakness.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: And in Wano, that lesson echoes when Zoro cuts through things no ordinary blade should touch.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: Unless he saw something in Zoro, and I think that's what Oda has been building for a long time.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: Chapter 1194 gives us the clearest look at it. In a flashback, Mihawk talks to Zoro about Conqueror's Haki.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: I think the lesson is about control: that Haki comes from your own strength, and you have to aim it.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: Zoro does it against Shepherd Sommers, and for the first time, the Haki flows through all three swords.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: He coats all three swords, and one of them is Kuina's.

shot.search: Zoro Sommers three swords Supreme King Haki
shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: Wado Ichimonji, a dead girl's sword, is one of the three blades carrying that Haki.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: Now strip all of that away. No Baratie loss means no Kuraigana, no lesson, no control over that Haki.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: And that control is what Elbaph needed against a Knight of God nobody could keep down.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: That's a regenerating Knight of God with no one in the whole crew who knows how to stop him.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: Mihawk stays champion of the sword, in a castle that never got a student, and the title never moves.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: A title that never moves sounds safe, but a world with nobody chasing the top is a world that stops getting stronger.

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: And that's a very dangerous thing to have in a story where Imu is still sending his own Knights after the giants...

shot.fallback: stone castle on a misty island with a lone swordsman looking out

lines.text: Elbaph is where all these threads land. It's a land of giants, and Imu's pact holders are hunting there.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: Imu reaches Elbaph through Gunko, and he already used Domi Reversi on Luffy and Loki back in chapter 1178.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: Dorry and Brogy, the two giants who fought for a hundred years, are the ones standing in front of Elbaph.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: Loki is starting his hybrid form, and Luffy is out of stamina after a joint hit on Imu in chapters 1191 to 1193.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: That's the setup in canon, and the one piece the Straw Hats needed was somebody who could deal with a Knight.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: In 1193, Zoro realizes Sommers' weak point is the steel heart and tries a Haki thrust, but he's still practicing.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: Then 1194 shows him learning to control that Haki through all three swords.

shot.search: Knight of God steel heart Sommers
shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: In this story, that discovery never happens, because Zoro never learned what Conqueror's Haki actually asks of him.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: Sommers is not a boss you out-muscle. Hit him with raw strength, and he just heals through it.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: I think the Knights of God are Imu's insurance. If nobody can kill them, nobody can reach him.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: That's my read, not canon: Mihawk's lesson is the first real crack in Imu's armor.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: So Sommers keeps regenerating, and every giant that swings at him just wastes a hit.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: Sanji is still stuck on Killingham, and Luffy is still out of gas, and nobody else has the answer.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: I think Loki is the only person with the strength to hold the line, and he does it for his father Harald.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: Meanwhile, I think Imu doesn't need to fight head on. He can keep hijacking people, the way he did with Gunko.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: And Dorry and Brogy hold their ground for the one reason they ever had, which is each other.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: Maybe that's enough to buy a few hours, but not enough to win a war.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: People will say Luffy would still find a way, because Luffy always finds a way, and I get that argument.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: But Luffy's way has always been to trust that his crew covers the part he can't cover himself.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: Luffy and Loki hurt Imu together, but hurting him isn't the same as cutting off what keeps him standing.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: This time the one he trusts most isn't there, and I don't think a rubber punch fixes that.

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: So the Knights of God stay immortal, and Imu gets his Elbaph back without ever stepping onto the field...

shot.fallback: giant village burning under a dark sky, giant warriors in the foreground

lines.text: Here's my read on the whole thing. Zoro surviving Mihawk is not a lucky escape. It's the first move in a chain.

shot.fallback: Zoro silhouette holding three swords at dawn

lines.text: Baratie leads to Kuraigana, Kuraigana leads to the lesson, and the lesson leads to a Haki a Knight of God has to respect.

shot.fallback: Zoro silhouette holding three swords at dawn

lines.text: Look at what Mihawk actually did. He cut Zoro down, and then he let the sea give him back.

shot.fallback: Zoro silhouette holding three swords at dawn

lines.text: Take away the first link, and you also take away the girl's sword in Zoro's mouth, the promise to Luffy, and the title.

shot.fallback: Zoro silhouette holding three swords at dawn

lines.text: That's the part I find so strange. Zoro's biggest loss may be the most important thing that ever happened to Elbaph.

shot.fallback: Zoro silhouette holding three swords at dawn

lines.text: The title Zoro chases is half Kuina's promise and half Mihawk's shadow, and he needed both.

shot.fallback: Zoro silhouette holding three swords at dawn

lines.text: So the next time somebody says Zoro's loss at the Baratie was nothing, tell them to read chapter 1194 again.

shot.fallback: Zoro silhouette holding three swords at dawn

lines.text: It also changes how I see Luffy, because his strength has always depended on trusting someone to cover his back.

shot.fallback: Zoro silhouette holding three swords at dawn

lines.text: My verdict: without Zoro at the Baratie, the Straw Hats still reach Elbaph. But they arrive with no answer to the Knights of God.

shot.fallback: Zoro silhouette holding three swords at dawn

lines.text: And the reason Zoro lives is that Mihawk decided a swordsman who refused to back down was worth sparing.

shot.fallback: Zoro silhouette holding three swords at dawn

lines.text: It's one decision at the Baratie that ends up deciding who can answer a Knight of God.

shot.fallback: Zoro silhouette holding three swords at dawn

lines.text: And if you want to see the crew when Luffy never eats the Gum-Gum Fruit, that's the story I told earlier this week.
